                    ### Question
                    A 42-year-old man comes to the physician for 1 month of worsening right knee pain. He has not had any trauma other than stubbing his toe 3 days ago at the garage where he works as a mechanic. Examination of the right knee shows swelling and erythema with fluctuance over the inferior patella. There is tenderness on palpation of the patella but no joint line tenderness or warmth. The range of flexion is limited because of the pain. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Inflammation of the patellar tendon
opb. Noninflammatory degeneration of the joint
opc. Infection of the joint
opd. Deposition of crystals in the joint
ope. Inflammation of periarticular fluid-filled sac

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's symptoms of right knee pain, swelling, erythema, and fluctuance over the inferior patella suggest a joint effusion, which is commonly associated with inflammation or infection. The absence of joint line tenderness and the minor nature of the recent toe injury make a meniscal injury less likely. The presence of fluctuance indicates fluid accumulation, which could be due to either infection or inflammation of the periarticular structures, such as bursitis. Given the clinical presentation, the most likely underlying cause is inflammation of a periarticular fluid-filled sac (bursitis), as it aligns with the symptoms observed and is a common cause of knee swelling without significant trauma. Other options, such as infection of the joint or crystal deposition, are less likely based on the absence of systemic symptoms or a history suggestive of gout. Therefore, the best-supported interpretation is that the patient's symptoms are due to inflammation of the periarticular fluid-filled sac.
